title: FCC chair warns media not to run the "fake polls" Trump keeps complaining about
gist: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr warned broadcasters against airing 'fake polls' after a hoax pollster, Wedgewood Polls, admitted fabricating data that had been added to aggregators including the New York Times, FiftyPlusOne and VoteHub; former FCC chairs and officials called Carr's warning an attempt at self-censorship.

insights.claim: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr warned broadcasters to avoid News Distortions or Broadcast Hoaxes by airing polls lacking scientific basis, without naming specific polls or broadcasters.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Vague regulatory warnings put broadcast licenses at leverage in editorial disputes.
insights.locator: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr today warned

insights.claim: In August Trump demanded the FCC punish or rebuke an NBC journalist and wrote the FCC must act on 'THE FAKE POLLS USED BY OUR CROOKED MEDIA'; Carr's vagueness may serve the ongoing battle against the media.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Regulatory pressure on broadcasters aligns with presidential media complaints.
insights.locator: Carr’s post did not mention any specific fake polls

insights.claim: Former FCC chairs Tom Wheeler and Mark Fowler and seven other former officials said good-faith reporting on public polls, even fabricated ones, does not violate the news distortion or hoax rules and that the FCC has zero authority to dictate editorial decisions.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Bipartisan former-regulator pushback signals legal contestability of Carr's approach.

insights.claim: Carr has spent two years threatening broadcast licenses and opening investigations of news companies disfavored by Trump, including a proceeding threatening the licenses of ABC-owned stations.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: License-risk overhang for media owners with broadcast licenses.
insights.locator: Carr’s latest warning to broadcasters came as no surprise

insights.claim: Commissioner Anna Gomez, the only Democrat on the FCC, said pollsters who intentionally mislead should answer for it but broadcasters reporting public polling data in good faith should never be punished.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.locator: Anna Gomez, the only Democratic commissioner

insights.claim: Wedgewood Polls admitted it fabricated polling data to test whether media and aggregators would report data without verifying the firm, and said it was added to aggregators including the NYT, FiftyPlusOne and VoteHub.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Poll aggregation pipelines can be gamed by plausible fake entrants.
insights.locator: An entity called Wedgewood Polls said yesterday

insights.claim: The aggregators Wedgewood named are not licensed broadcasters, relevant because Carr says he uses FCC authority only over licensed broadcasters using public spectrum.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The hoax involved outlets outside FCC jurisdiction, weakening the regulatory link.

insights.claim: FiftyPlusOne, the NYT and VoteHub say they vetted Wedgewood: FiftyPlusOne confirmed a named founder had polling experience, VoteHub graded it D, and the NYT used 15 Wedgewood polls only for state and congressional-district races.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Vetting processes were applied but still failed to detect fabrication.
insights.locator: NYT and VoteHub explain poll inclusion

insights.claim: The NYT said Wedgewood polls were never in its Trump approval or national congressional-control averages, and it never included results from Median Strategies, another group that admitted faking results as a social experiment earlier this year.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: National averages were insulated, limiting market-moving distortion.

insights.claim: Nate Silver removed Wedgewood from his polling site and said its polls leaned about 1 percentage point more favorable to Democrats than other polls.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Effect size of the fabricated data on averages was small.
insights.locator: Nate Silver removed Wedgewood from his polling site today.
